notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in it counts as correct for this topic_id.

This is a SECOND, independent synthetic application (Vantage Digital Forensics Group, LLC) against the same true_requirements.json as data/SHOP-PR-26-002435 -- built to add SFT/eval training data with deliberately different failure and compliance shapes from the original application (Meridian Forensic Solutions, LLC).

The original application left all 15 individually-split hardware-detail topics (dedicated NVMe drives x4, hot-swap bays x3, USB hubs x2, chassis specs x6) completely unaddressed, scoring insufficient_information/non_compliant uniformly. This application includes a full itemized configuration addressing every one of them, producing genuine variety: 12 clean compliant matches, one config decision (a shared processing/database NVMe drive) that cleanly fails two related requirements at once (a realistic single-root-cause double failure, mirrored by fixing the top-level ram_capacity_spec and warranty_spec failures from the original to compliant instead), one vague hot-swap-bay mention with no confirmable tray count (insufficient_information), and a new USB-hub port-count contradiction between the itemized spec and a rear-panel summary elsewhere in the same document (contradictory) -- replacing the GPU contradiction, which remains the canonical example for that topic in the original application.

item_identification_completeness, pricing_inclusive_of_all_charges, and quote_validity_through_sept30 are inverted to compliant (fully itemized/inclusive/dated correctly) rather than the original's incomplete-identification, unconfirmed-inclusive-pricing, and mismatched-validity-period failures.
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone.

primary_verdict / primary_verdict_source (added by SFT data-prep pass): a single training-target label per topic, additive -- acceptable_verdicts is unchanged and remains the source of truth for verdict-accuracy scoring. primary_verdict is the pipeline's own correct prediction where one exists (source: pipeline_prediction), else acceptable_verdicts[0] (source: acceptable_verdicts_first). null for topics with acceptable_verdicts: null (excluded from SFT training, same as they're excluded from verdict scoring).
